name: JS1/forum-search
top_fix: VERIFICATION.md and six chapters describe a tested scenario ('six threads, delete its only item, page 2 clamps to page 1 with five rows, total five') that does not exist in test/feature.test.ts (3 threads, pageSize 2, no delete, page 2 with 1 item, total 3). Rewrite that sentence everywhere it appears, or add the test.
summary: The strongest pagination change in the batch: the original derived total from COUNT(*) OVER() on the returned rows, so any page past the end reported zero; Astra replaced it with a separate COUNT plus the page query inside one REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY transaction, a page clamp, and a t.id ASC tie-breaker after ts_rank/created_at. Tests prove ordering stability across repeated calls and that five malformed POSTs leave the thread count unchanged. The line-34 excerpt is exact, but the 'Tested behavior' narrative repeated in seven files is invented, which is a D6 problem.

name: JS1/invoice-studio
top_fix: Rewrite at least two sections of astraupskill/02-CONCEPTS.md to be about money and dates in this codebase (numeric vs JS number, why Math.round(x*100)/100 is needed, what /^\d+(?:\.\d{1,2})?$/ accepts) instead of the boilerplate shared verbatim with 47 other courses.
summary: Best input-contract lesson in the batch. Invoices now require a UUID client, a real calendar issue date (2027-02-29 is rejected via ISO round-trip), at most 100 lines, whole safe-integer quantities, two-decimal prices and tax 0-100; the total rounds to cents. Three tests: an arithmetic case (0.1 x 2 @ 10% -> 0.22), seven adversarial payloads followed by a deepEqual against the stored invoice, and a PL/pgSQL BEFORE INSERT trigger that fails a line insert after the old lines were deleted, proving the whole PUT rolls back. Everything on disk matches the course; the weakness is templated prose, stub exercises and minified tests.

name: JS1/asset-checkout
top_fix: The fixture the course tells you to build (an asset titled 'Camera kit for field interviews', VERIFICATION.md:18 and six chapters) does not exist; test/workflow.test.ts:7 uses 'A lesson record'. Align the prose with the test, then promote the schema.sql seed bug and the pg DATE type-parser into their own 02-CONCEPTS.md section.
summary: The most complete course in the batch and the one with the most real engineering: Astra found a genuine pre-existing seed bug (json_to_recordset matched the unquoted column due_date instead of the JSON key dueDate, so every seeded due date was NULL), added pg.types.setTypeParser(1082, v => v) so DATE columns stay calendar strings, made PATCH /status row-locked and idempotent with its audit insert in the same transaction, and put COUNT and the page query under REPEATABLE READ with a clamp and an id tie-breaker. Four tests including a trigger-based rollback test that drops the trigger and re-verifies success. Fabricated fixture title and heavy template reuse are the deductions.
